idiom_name: return unless cond / raise ... unless cond modifier guards
implementation_notes: Ruby's guard shape is the modifier statement documented in the control-expressions reference: return unless connected, raise ArgumentError, "..." unless valid?, next unless item.ready? in loops - the condition trails the action, which replaces the nested if/else that would otherwise wrap the rest of the method. Methods return their last expression, so a bare return exits with nil while return value or x or return supply a default. For multi-requirement admission bands, keep one modifier per requirement; anything more involved belongs in a private validate! method.
code_sketch:
def publish(draft)
  raise ArgumentError, "draft required" unless draft     # guard: bad input
  return draft.to_h if draft.published?                  # guard: idempotent exit
  raise "draft not ready" unless draft.ready_at <= Time.now
  repo.publish(draft)                                    # happy path stays flat
end
pitfalls: Modifier parse order surprises: p a if a = fetch reads a as a method before the assignment is parsed; assign first, then guard.
return inside a block (each/map) exits the enclosing method, not just the block; use next/break inside iteration guards.
unless with an else reads backwards; prefer if/else or two separate guards.
